# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

# Circular SYN-7421/13/2025: Related Party Transaction Approval Thresholds under LODR

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to listed entities whose equity shares are traded on a recognised stock exchange. It governs related party transactions (RPTs) entered into by the entity or any of its subsidiaries, including transactions involving transfer of resources, services, or obligations, and any indemnity, guarantee, or escrow arrangement with a related party.

## 2. Approval Thresholds

An RPT exceeding the lower of 2.5 per cent of annual consolidated turnover or INR 1,200 crore requires prior approval of the audit committee and a special resolution of the shareholders. Transactions below this threshold require audit committee approval only. Transactions with a value below INR 10 crore, or below 0.5 per cent of turnover, are exempt from shareholder approval but must be reported quarterly.

## 3. Interested Party Controls

A related party, or any director with a material interest, shall abstain from voting on the relevant resolution. Listed entities shall maintain documented controls, including a withholding of payment pending approval where the transaction has not been cleared, and a fortnightly reconciliation of RPT ledgers.

## 4. Disclosure and Penalties

Entities shall disclose approved RPTs to the exchanges within 2 working days of the approval date. Non-compliance attracts a penalty of INR 25 lakh per instance, with an additional INR 50,000 per day of delay, capped at INR 1 crore per financial year.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026 for transactions entered into on or after that date. Existing arrangements shall be brought into compliance by 30 September 2026.

# Beneficial Owner Identification for Corporate Customers

## Penalty Exposure (Flagged First)

- **RBI Regulated Entity penalty:** Failure to comply with Para 12, 16 or 24 attracts a monetary penalty of up to Rs 1 crore per contravention on the Regulated Entity, in addition to any action under the PMLA [GRC-01, Para 41].
- **PMLA Rules penalty:** For each failure to comply with the PMLA Rules, FIU-IND may impose a penalty of Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per failure [GRC-02, Section 13]. Rule 9 incorporates the beneficial-owner requirement by reference [GRC-02, Rule 9].
- **Live exposure at Meridian Finance Ltd:** Risk R-12 (failure to identify beneficial owners of company customers) carries HIGH residual risk because control IC-KYC-07 operates on the superseded 25% threshold [GRC-04, R-12]. Any onboarding or periodic-review records built on that threshold are exposed to the Para 41 penalty above.

## 1. Who Must Be Identified

Where the customer is a company, the RE must identify the **beneficial owner**, defined as every **natural person** who, alone or with others, either:
- holds ownership of or entitlement to the qualifying stake in the shares or capital, or
- exercises control through other means [GRC-01, Para 16].

Entities such as holding companies are not themselves the beneficial owner. The obligation is to trace through to natural persons.

## 2. What Ownership Stake Counts

- **Current threshold: 10% or more** of the shares or capital [GRC-01, Para 16].
- **Superseded threshold: 25%** was withdrawn from 1 July 2025 [GRC-01, Para 16]. Any control or procedure still using 25% does not meet the current requirement.
- The test covers stakes held "alone or with others," so aggregated holdings of several natural persons are relevant [GRC-01, Para 16].

## 3. Fallback Where No Natural Person Is Identified

Where no natural person is identified under the test above, the **senior managing official** is treated as the beneficial owner [GRC-01, Para 16]. The file should document why no natural person met the test before applying this fallback.

## 4. Timing and Refresh

- Customer due diligence applies at account opening and whenever there is doubt about previously obtained identification data [GRC-01, Para 12].
- Beneficial-owner data is part of periodic updation: at least every 2 years for high-risk, 8 years for medium-risk and 10 years for low-risk customers [GRC-01, Para 24].
- Identity and transaction records are preserved for 5 years after the business relationship ends [GRC-02, Rule 9].

## 5. Control Mapping to Obligations

| Control / Test | Regulatory Obligation Satisfied | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| IC-KYC-07: BO identification at onboarding and periodic updation [GRC-04, R-12] | Para 16 (BO, 10% threshold); Para 24 (periodic updation) [GRC-04, R-12] | **Design gap:** operates on the 25% threshold, which has been withdrawn. Residual risk HIGH. |
| SOP-IA-KYC-03, Step 4: verify BO identified at the 10% threshold [GRC-05, Steps 4] | Para 16 [GRC-05, Step 4] | Appropriate test design. It will flag exceptions if the control is still on 25%. |

## Answer: Events Permitting Buyer Termination Before Closing

The only termination right identified in the corpus is the Material Adverse Change (MAC) clause. Under it, the Buyer may terminate before Closing without liability if either limb is triggered:

1. **Earnings decline:** a reduction of more than 15% in consolidated EBITDA measured against the last audited financial year [DEAL-01, Clause 11(a)].
2. **Regulatory licence action:** any regulatory action that revokes or suspends the licence of Meridian Finance Ltd, the NBFC subsidiary [DEAL-01, Clause 11(b); DEAL-01, Parties and Target].

The termination right applies only where "a MAC occurs before Closing" [DEAL-01, Clause 11]. The Expected Closing date is 30 June 2026 [DEAL-01, Purchase Price].

### Observations for Risk Review

- **MAC threshold:** Limb (a) is a percentage test. The extract does not define "consolidated EBITDA" or set out the calculation method, so the measurement basis is open to dispute.
- **Limb (b) scope:** The trigger is "any regulatory action" that revokes or suspends the licence. The extract does not define "regulatory action" beyond the revocation or suspension wording, and it does not address partial restrictions, conditions, or pending proceedings.
- **Exposure context:** The Purchase Price is Rs 1,200 crore for 100% of the shares [DEAL-01, Purchase Price]. A 15% EBITDA shortfall is the only quantified MAC threshold in the extract.
- **Post-closing protections are not walk-away rights:** The general warranty indemnity is capped at Rs 240 crore (20%), subject to a Rs 6 crore basket (0.5%), with claims notifiable within 24 months of Closing [DEAL-01, Clause 9.2]. The tax indemnity is uncapped, carries no basket, and survives 7 years after Closing [DEAL-01, Clause 9.4]. The Rs 120 crore escrow (10%) is held for 18 months after Closing as security for indemnity claims [DEAL-01, Clause 10]. None of these operates as a pre-completion exit, and the extract does not say whether they apply to pre-closing breaches.
- **Conditions precedent:** Clause 12 lists three CPs: (a) a Registered Valuer's report under the Companies Act 2013; (b) FEMA pricing compliance and filing of Form FC-TRS; and (c) FCRA compliance regarding Meridian Foundation's shares [DEAL-01, Clause 12]. The extract does not state that failure of a CP entitles the Buyer to terminate without liability. Whether a CP failure is a walk-away event therefore cannot be confirmed from the corpus.
- **Regulatory approval standstill:** DIST-28 states that parties must not close or integrate operations until approval is received [DIST-28, Section 2], and that a combination must be notified within 30 calendar days of signing or the trigger event, whichever is earlier [DIST-28, Section 2]. DIST-28 is a synthetic benchmarking note and does not address SPA termination rights. Whether a failed or delayed competition clearance allows the Buyer to withdraw is not stated in the corpus.

---

## Gaps / Not found in corpus

- **Long-stop date:** No outside date for termination is given in the extract.
- **Cure periods or notice mechanics:** The extract does not specify whether the Buyer must give notice, or whether the Sellers can cure a MA

# Advisory Note on Combination Notification Thresholds and Review Timelines, SYN-4417/28/2025

## 1. Asset and Turnover Thresholds
A proposed combination must be notified where the combined assets in India of the parties exceed INR 9,000 million, or their combined turnover in India exceeds INR 27,500 million. A group-level test applies at combined assets of INR 36,000 million or combined turnover of INR 110,000 million. A de minimis exemption is available where the target holds assets in India below INR 3,500 million.

## 2. Filing Window and Standstill
Notice in the prescribed form must be filed within 30 calendar days of signing the definitive agreement or the trigger event, whichever is earlier. Parties must not close the transaction or integrate operations until approval is received.

## 3. Review Timelines
The Authority shall form a prima facie opinion within 30 working days of receipt of a complete filing. Where it calls for further information, the clock stops and restarts on receipt of the response. The outer limit for a final order is 150 days from filing.

## 4. Penalties and Indemnities
Failure to notify attracts a penalty of up to 1 per cent of the turnover or assets of the parties, whichever is higher. Transaction documents commonly provide for an escrow of 5 per cent of the consideration, and an indemnity for regulatory costs capped at 2 per cent of enterprise value.

## 5. Circular Reference
Parties should monitor circular SYN-CCI/12/2025, dated 1 April 2025, for revised filing forms and fee schedules.

The scheme applies to a compromise or arrangement between a company and its members or creditors. Approval requires a majority in number, representing at least 70% in value, of those present and voting at the convened meeting. Each class must be separately convened where rights differ materially.

## 2. Filing and Notice Periods

A petition is filed before the Tribunal with a fee of ₹38,500. Notice to the Regional Director and the Official Liquidator must issue within 14 days of filing. Members and creditors receive at least 21 clear days' notice before the meeting, and the notification to the stock exchange must be lodged by 3 March 2025 under circular No. SYN-MCA/12/2025.

## 3. Withholding, Indemnity and Escrow Controls

Where consideration is payable to dissenting shareholders, 2.5% is placed in escrow for 180 days. A 1.5% withholding applies to deemed transfers. The acquirer's indemnity is capped at 10% of the transaction value, with a survival period of 24 months.

## 4. Penalties and Non-Compliance

Failure to file the scheme within the prescribed window attracts a default penalty of ₹75,000, plus ₹2,000 per day of continuing default, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh. Directors of the company are liable jointly for the penalty unless they establish that they acted diligently.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

## 2. Duty Rate and Valuation Floor

Share transfer instruments are chargeable at 0.15 per cent of the consideration or the market value of the shares, whichever is higher. Duty on any single instrument shall not fall below ₹250 or exceed ₹1,20,000. Where shares are transferred through a demat account without a separate instrument, the depository participant shall withhold and remit duty on behalf of the transferor within 7 working days.

## 3. Agreements to Sell and Escrow Arrangements

An agreement to sell attracts duty at 0.05 per cent of the agreed consideration. Where part of the consideration is held in escrow, duty is payable on the full amount at the time of execution, and any indemnity or holdback amount must be disclosed in the agreement.

## 4. Impounding and Penalty

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

# Advisory Note SYN-RPT/41/2025: Approvals for Related Party Transactions under Section 188

## 1. Scope and Trigger Thresholds

This note covers contracts or arrangements with related parties that fall within Section 188 of the fictional Companies Act, 2013 framework. Under the illustrative model, a transaction exceeding 10 percent of turnover, or 20 percent of net worth, requires a special resolution of members, with the interested director and related parties abstaining from voting.

All related party transactions require prior approval of the Audit Committee. Where the Committee's approval is sought after execution, a ratification window of 60 days applies. Board minutes must record the basis of arm's length pricing, supported by a benchmarking study dated within 90 days of approval.

Non-compliance attracts a penalty of ₹5,00,000 on the company and ₹1,00,000 on each responsible officer, with a further daily default fee of ₹10,000. Companies should adopt a written related party policy, circulated by the Company Secretary by 31 March 2026, and obtain an indemnity from interested directors for losses arising from undisclosed arrangements. # Buyer Walk-Away Rights Before Completion: Axiom / Meridian SPA

## Summary

The SPA extract provides **one** express pre-closing termination right: a Material Adverse Change (MAC) under Clause 11. If a MAC occurs before Closing, the Buyer may terminate "without liability" [DEAL-01, Clause 11]. The extract does not contain any other express walk-away event.

## 1. Material Adverse Change (MAC), Clause 11

A MAC is defined as either of the following [DEAL-01, Clause 11]:

| Limb | Trigger | Measurement / Threshold |
|---|---|---|
| **(a) Earnings decline** | Reduction in consolidated EBITDA | More than **15%** against the last audited financial year |
| **(b) Regulatory action** | Any regulatory action that revokes or suspends the licence of **Meridian Finance Ltd** (the NBFC subsidiary) | Binary; any revocation or suspension |

**Consequence:** If a MAC occurs before Closing, the Buyer may terminate the Agreement without liability [DEAL-01, Clause 11].

**Exposure threshold:** The 15% EBITDA reduction is the quantitative trigger. Applied to the last audited base, it is the point at which the Buyer's exit right crystallises.

## 2. Application to Known Due Diligence Findings

The DD memo does not identify any current event that meets a MAC limb:

- **Finding 1 (Section 94Z withholding, Rs 4.2 crore tax plus interest and 100% penalty exposure) [DEAL-05, Finding 1]:** This is a tax liability, not an EBITDA reduction or a licence action. It is addressed through the tax indemnity in Clause 9.4 [DEAL-01, Clause 9.4] and the pre-31 March 2026 payment recommendation [DEAL-05, Recommendations].

**Assessment:** On the current record, none of the DD findings constitutes a MAC. The Buyer's exit route would need a fresh EBITDA test or a licence action.

# SYN-HPL/SHA-41/26/2025: Shareholders Agreement Summary, Helix Pharma Ltd

## 1. Drag-Along Right

Where Promoter Group holders intend to transfer shares representing 58% or more of paid-up equity capital, they may require the remaining shareholders to sell pro rata on identical terms. A drag notice shall be issued at least 30 days before the proposed completion date. Any indemnity given by a dragged shareholder is capped at the consideration that shareholder receives.

## 2. Tag-Along Right

Minority shareholders holding not more than 10% may elect to sell their full holding alongside any Promoter transfer that results in a change of control. The election must be communicated in writing within 14 days of the transfer notice. Five percent of the purchase price shall be held in escrow for 90 days against warranty claims.

## 3. Board Reserved Matters

The following require the affirmative vote of the Investor Director in addition to a simple majority of the Board:

(a) issue of equity or convertible instruments exceeding ₹75 crore in any financial year;
(b) related-party transactions above ₹4 crore;
(c) borrowings exceeding 1.5 times net worth;
(d) any regulatory filing involving renewal of a product licence.

## 4. Default and Penalties

Breach of a reserved matter control attracts a penalty of 2% per month on the amount affected, accruing from the date of breach until cure. Persistent non-compliance for two consecutive quarters entitles the Investor to nominate an additional independent director, effective on notice to the Company Secretary dated 1 April 2026.

An acquirer crossing a fictional aggregate voting share threshold of 31 per cent of the target's equity capital, whether directly or through persons acting in concert, must make a public announcement within 2 working days. Creeping acquisitions of up to 2 per cent in any financial year are excluded from the trigger, subject to the controls in Section 4.

## 2. Offer Size and Minimum Price
The offer covers a fictional 26 per cent of expanded voting capital. The offer price is the highest of (a) the negotiated price under the triggering agreement, (b) the 60-trading-day volume-weighted average price, and (c) the highest price paid by the acquirer in the preceding 26 weeks. Where the target's shares are thinly traded, a fictional independent valuation report must accompany the offer, and the escrow deposit must equal 25 per cent of the consideration payable up to the first ₹500 crore.

## 3. Escrow, Withholding and Indemnity
Cash or bank guarantee escrow is placed with a designated escrow bank before the detailed public statement is published. A fictional withholding of 10 per cent of the offer consideration may be retained against unresolved demands arising from the target's pre-offer disclosures, backed by an indemnity from the promoter group capped at ₹75 crore.

## 4. Penalties and Circular Compliance
Failure to make the public announcement attracts a fictional penalty of ₹1 lakh per day of delay, subject to a ceiling of ₹25 crore. Voting rights in excess of the trigger stay suspended until cure. Compliance must be evidenced under Circular SYN-SEBI/OO/09/2025, effective 1 April 2026.

# FEMA NDI Rules - synthetic extract

## Pricing
A transfer of shares of an Indian company from a resident to a non-resident shall not be at a price less than the fair value determined under an internationally accepted pricing methodology. The fair value shall be certified by a Chartered Accountant, a SEBI-registered merchant banker or a Registered Valuer.

## Deferred consideration and escrow
Up to **25% of the total consideration** may be deferred or held in escrow for a period not exceeding **18 months** from the date of the transfer agreement.

## Reporting
The resident seller or Indian company shall file **Form FC-TRS** with the authorised dealer bank within **60 days** of receipt of the consideration or transfer of shares, whichever is earlier.
Delay attracts compounding under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.

## Sectoral condition
Where the Indian company has a regulated financial subsidiary (such as an NBFC), prior approval of the sectoral regulator may be required for change in control.

# SYN-4471/23/2025: Advisory Note on Schemes of Arrangement and Merger Approvals

This note summarises fictional procedural controls for schemes proposed under a notional Section 230 framework. It is intended for internal review only.

## 1. Scope and Meeting Thresholds

The scheme applies to a compromise or arrangement between a company and its members or creditors. Approval requires a majority in number, representing at least 70% in value, of those present and voting at the convened meeting. Each class must be separately convened where rights differ materially.

## 2. Filing and Notice Periods

A petition is filed before the Tribunal with a fee of ₹38,500. Notice to the Regional Director and the Official Liquidator must issue within 14 days of filing. Members and creditors receive at least 21 clear days' notice before the meeting, and the notification to the stock exchange must be lodged by 3 March 2025 under circular No. SYN-MCA/12/2025.

## 3. Withholding, Indemnity and Escrow Controls

Where consideration is payable to dissenting shareholders, 2.5% is placed in escrow for 180 days. A 1.5% withholding applies to deemed transfers. The acquirer's indemnity is capped at 10% of the transaction value, with a survival period of 24 months.

Failure to file the scheme within the prescribed window attracts a default penalty of ₹75,000, plus ₹2,000 per day of continuing default, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh. Directors of the company are liable jointly for the penalty unless they establish that they acted diligently.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

## 2. Duty Rate and Valuation Floor

Share transfer instruments are chargeable at 0.15 per cent of the consideration or the market value of the shares, whichever is higher. Duty on any single instrument shall not fall below ₹250 or exceed ₹1,20,000. Where shares are transferred through a demat account without a separate instrument, the depository participant shall withhold and remit duty on behalf of the transferor within 7 working days.

## 3. Agreements to Sell and Escrow Arrangements

An agreement to sell attracts duty at 0.05 per cent of the agreed consideration. Where part of the consideration is held in escrow, duty is payable on the full amount at the time of execution, and any indemnity or holdback amount must be disclosed in the agreement.

## 4. Impounding and Penalty

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

Breach of a reserved matter control attracts a penalty of 2% per month on the amount affected, accruing from the date of breach until cure. records.answer:
## Answer

Documents that distribute head-office input tax credit (ITC) to branches are **ISD invoices**. From **1 January 2026**, each ISD invoice must carry an **Invoice Reference Number (IRN) and a QR code**. The corpus does not describe a separate "electronic bill identifier" for this purpose; the IRN is the identifier.

## Analysis

**1. The document type is the ISD invoice.**
Credit may be distributed to branches or distinct persons only through an ISD invoice issued by a registered Input Service Distributor. Distribution by ordinary invoice, journal entry, or internal debit note is not valid [TAX-03, Section 2]. The ISD must first hold registration under Rule 39A [TAX-03, Section 1].

**2. The identifier and QR requirement.**
ISD invoices must carry an IRN and QR code from 1 January 2026 [TAX-04, Section 3]. The IRN is generated on the Invoice Registration Portal, and every e-invoice must carry an IRN and QR code [TAX-04, Section 2].

**3. Consequence of omitting the IRN.**
Invoices without an IRN are not valid for claiming input tax credit by the recipient [TAX-04, Section 2]. This is a direct transactional risk for the receiving branch, which would be denied the credit.

**4. Prospective vs. retrospective status.**
- **ISD registration requirement:** Prospective, effective 1 April 2025, expressly labelled as such [TAX-03, Section 1].
- **IRN and QR code on ISD invoices:** Prospective. The source gives an effective date of 1 January 2026 and imposes no retrospective effect. The source does not use the label "prospective" for this provision, so the characterisation is inferred from the effective date.

**5. Penalties and exposure.**
- Failure to issue an e-invoice attracts a penalty of 100% of tax due or ₹10,000, whichever is higher, per invoice [TAX-04, Section 5].
- Credit distributed without ISD registration or an ISD invoice is denied to the recipient unit. Wrongly availed credit is recoverable with interest at 18% per annum, and a penalty of ₹25,000 applies per instance [TAX-03, Section 3].

**6. Interaction with the e-invoicing threshold.**
E-invoicing is mandatory for registered persons with Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) above ₹5 crore, effective 1 January 2026 [TAX-04, Section 1; TAX-05]. TAX-04 Section 3 applies the IRN and QR requirement to ISD invoices without stating an AATO threshold. Read literally, the ISD IRN obligation is not conditional on turnover. Controllers should confirm this reading before relying on it.

## Caveats on Sources

- TAX-04, TAX-03, and TAX-05 are labelled in the corpus as synthetic benchmarking documents, not official Council records or CBIC circulars. Any position taken with a client must be verified against the official gazette or circular text before use.
- TAX-05 is a summary table and restates the e-invoicing requirement without addressing ISD invoices specifically

# Ruling of the 57th GST Council Meeting

## 1. E-invoicing threshold (prospective)
E-invoicing becomes mandatory for every registered person whose Aggregate Annual Turnover (AATO) exceeds Rs 5 crore, down from Rs 10 crore, with effect from 1 January 2026.

## 2. Invoice Reference Number and QR code
Every e-invoice must carry an Invoice Reference Number (IRN) generated on the Invoice Registration Portal, and a QR code. Invoices without an IRN are not valid for claiming input tax credit by the recipient.

## 3. ISD invoices
ISD invoices issued under Circular SYN-CBIC/203/2025 for distribution of input tax credit must also carry an IRN and QR code from 1 January 2026.

## 4. Reporting window
Taxpayers with AATO of Rs 10 crore and above must report invoices to the portal within 30 days of the invoice date.

## 5. Penalty
Failure to issue an e-invoice attracts a penalty of 100% of the tax due or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, per invoice.

# Circular SYN-7741/8/2025: Customs Valuation of Related-Party Imports

## 1. Scope
This circular applies to imports where buyer and seller are related persons. Where the declared transaction value is accepted under the related-party test, the proper officer shall examine whether the relationship has influenced price.

## 2. Contemporaneous Price Comparison
Importers shall furnish comparable import data for the preceding 90 days. Where the declared value falls more than 12 per cent below the average of contemporaneous unrelated-party prices, the declaration shall be provisionally rejected and a show-cause notice issued within 15 days.

## 3. Security and Escrow
Pending final determination, the importer may furnish a bank guarantee or deposit the duty differential into an escrow account at a notified bank. The security shall equal 110 per cent of the differential duty computed on the enhanced value.

## 4. Controls and Indemnity
Importers with related-party imports exceeding ₹50 crore in a financial year shall maintain a documented pricing control framework, reviewed by an independent auditor by 31 March 2026. Parties shall execute an indemnity covering duty, interest and penalty arising from valuation adjustments.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date
Knowing under-valuation shall attract a penalty of 100 per cent of the duty short-levied, subject to a floor of ₹2 lakh. This circular takes effect on 1 July 2025 and applies to bills of entry filed on or after that date.

# Electronic Identifier and QR Requirement for Head-Office Credit Distribution to Branches

## Direct Answer

Head-office credit distributed to branches must be documented through an **ISD invoice**. From **1 January 2026**, that ISD invoice must carry an **Invoice Reference Number (IRN)** and a **QR code** [TAX-04, Section 3]. The IRN and QR requirement is the same one that applies to e-invoices generally, and it is linked to the ISD framework in [TAX-03, Section 4].

## Analysis

**1. The distribution vehicle must be an ISD invoice.**
- Credit on common input services may be distributed to branches or distinct persons only by an ISD invoice issued by a registered Input Service Distributor [TAX-03, Section 1; Section 2].
- Distribution by ordinary invoice, journal entry, or internal debit note is not valid [TAX-03, Section 2].
- ISD registration under Rule 39A is mandatory for any registered person that distributes credit on common input services. This applies **prospectively from 1 April 2025** [TAX-03, Section 1].

**2. The identifier and QR requirement.**
- ISD invoices must carry an IRN and QR code **from 1 January 2026** [TAX-04, Section 3].
- Every e-invoice must carry an IRN, generated on the Invoice Registration Portal, and a QR code [TAX-04, Section 2].
- An invoice without an IRN is **not valid for the recipient to claim input tax credit** [TAX-04, Section 2]. For a branch receiving ISD credit, a missing IRN therefore puts the credit itself at risk.

**3. Consequences of non-compliance.**
- Credit distributed without ISD registration or without an ISD invoice is **denied to the recipient unit** [TAX-03, Section 3].
- Wrongly availed credit is recoverable **with interest at 18% per annum** [TAX-03, Section 3].
- A penalty of **Rs 25,000 per instance** applies [TAX-03, Section 3].
- Failure to issue an e-invoice attracts a penalty of **100% of tax due or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, per invoice** [TAX-04, Section 5]. The corpus does not expressly confirm that this penalty applies to ISD invoices (see Gaps).

**4. Prospective versus retrospective characterisation.**
- The ISD registration and ISD-invoice requirements are **prospective**, effective 1 April 2025 [TAX-03, Section 1].
- The IRN and QR requirement for ISD invoices is **prospective**, effective 1 January 2026 [TAX-04, Sections 1 and 3].
- The corpus contains **no retrospective clarification** on either point.

**5. Corpus limitation.**
- TAX-04 and TAX-03 are marked as **synthetic benchmarking documents, not official records**. The analysis above reflects only what those documents state.
- TAX-05 (the consolidated table) lists the e-invoicing row (AATO above Rs 5 crore) but does **not** mention ISD invoices [TAX-05, Table row "E-invoicing"].

## Gaps / Not found in corpus

- **Applicability of the AATO threshold to ISD invoices:** The corpus states the e-invoicing threshold (AATO above Rs 5 crore, from 1 January 2026) [TAX-04, Section 1]. It does not state whether the ISD IRN/QR obligation in TAX-04 Section 3 is subject to the same threshold, or applies to all ISD invoices regardless of turnover.

# Circular No. SYN-4417/6/2025: Refund of Unutilised Input Tax Credit under Inverted Duty Structure

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to registered persons whose input goods or services carry a higher rate of tax than the output supplies, resulting in accumulated unutilised input tax credit. It covers supplies made on or after 1 April 2025 and all refund claims filed under the fictional Notification No. 19/2025-Central Tax.

## 2. Computation of Refund

The refundable amount equals the unutilised credit attributable to inputs, multiplied by the ratio of net turnover of inverted-rated supplies to adjusted total turnover. Claims below Rs 25,000 in a tax period are not admissible.

## 3. Provisional Refund and Withholding

Officers may sanction up to 90 per cent of the claimed amount provisionally. The balance of 10 per cent shall be withheld pending verification, which must conclude within 60 days of filing. Where a discrepancy exceeding 5 per cent is found, the entire provisional amount may be recovered with interest at 18 per cent per annum.

## 4. Indemnity, Escrow and Internal Controls

Claimants seeking provisional refunds above Rs 2 crore must furnish a bank guarantee or deposit an escrow equal to 15 per cent of the excess, and execute an indemnity undertaking covering reversal of wrongful credit. Taxpayers shall maintain documented reconciliation controls and certify monthly ledger tie-outs.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date

A false or inflated refund claim attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax wrongly refunded, subject to a floor of Rs 10,000. This circular takes effect on 15 July 2025.

# Advisory Note SYN-CBIC/88/2025 on Composition Levy Eligibility for Small Manufacturers

## 1. Aggregate Turnover Ceiling

A registered person engaged in the manufacture of goods may opt for the composition levy where aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year does not exceed ₹96,00,000. For taxpayers in designated special-category States, the ceiling is ₹48,00,000. Turnover is computed on a PAN-wide basis for the purposes of this illustration.

## 2. Supply Restrictions

Composition dealers shall not make inter-State outward supplies or supplies through an e-commerce operator that collects tax at source. Supplies of specified edible preparations attract a fixed levy of 2.5 per cent of turnover in the State, effective from 1 April 2025 under Notification SYN-N/12/2025.

## 3. Option Filing and Reversal of Credit

Intimation in Form SYN-CMP/1 must be filed on or before 15 May 2025 for the current year. Where input tax credit has been availed on capital goods, a reversal equal to 10 per cent of the value of such goods is required on the date of opting in. Failure to reverse attracts a penalty of ₹25,000.

## 4. Loss of Eligibility and Liability Escrow

Where turnover exceeds the ceiling during a year, the person ceases to be eligible from the day the threshold is crossed and must pay tax at normal rates on stock held. Interest at 18 per cent per annum applies to delayed payment. Management is advised to maintain monthly turnover controls and an escrow reserve equal to 5 per cent of projected turnover against this contingent liability.

> **PENALTY FLAG (Maximum exposure):** Up to **Rs 1 crore per contravention** on the Regulated Entity for failure to comply with the beneficial-owner requirement in Para 16 [GRC-01, Para 41]. This is **in addition to** any action under the PMLA [GRC-01, Para 41]. A separate PMLA penalty of **Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per failure** may also apply [GRC-02, Section 13].

- **Beneficial-owner identification:** For a company customer, the RE must identify every natural person holding **10% or more** of shares or capital, or exercising control by other means. The earlier 25% threshold was withdrawn from 1 July 2025 [GRC-01, Para 16].
- **Fallback:** If no natural person is identified, the senior managing official is treated as the beneficial owner [GRC-01, Para 16].

# Master Direction SYN-RBI/KYC/2025 - Know Your Customer (KYC)

Issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to all Regulated Entities (REs), including banks and NBFCs. Read with the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) Rules.

## Para 12 - Customer Due Diligence (CDD)
REs shall carry out CDD at account opening, and whenever there is doubt about previously obtained identification data.

## Para 16 - Beneficial Owner (BO)
Where the customer is a company, the RE shall identify the beneficial owner: every natural person who, alone or with others, holds ownership of or entitlement to **10% or more** of the shares or capital, or who exercises control through other means.
The earlier threshold of 25% is withdrawn from 1 July 2025.
Where no natural person is identified, the senior managing official shall be treated as the beneficial owner.

## Para 24 - Periodic updation
KYC records shall be updated at least once every:
- 2 years for high-risk customers,
- 8 years for medium-risk customers,
- 10 years for low-risk customers.

## Para 41 - Penalty
Failure to comply with Para 12, 16 or 24 attracts a monetary penalty of up to Rs 1 crore per contravention on the Regulated Entity, in addition to any action under the PMLA.

## Para 45 - Reporting
Suspicious transactions shall be reported as required under the PMLA Rules to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

# SYN-ESG/11/2025: Registration Framework for ESG Rating Providers

## 1. Scope and Eligibility

This circular applies to any entity offering ESG rating services to listed entities or investors in India. An applicant must have a minimum net worth of Rs 8 crore in each of the three preceding financial years and must not have any director convicted of an offence involving moral turpitude.

## 2. Application and Fee

Applications shall be filed electronically in Form ESG-R within 45 days of this notification. A non-refundable processing fee of Rs 2,50,000 applies, and an additional Rs 1,00,000 is payable for each methodology submitted for review.

## 3. Governance and Controls

Each provider shall maintain at least two independent directors, an internal review committee, and an indemnity arrangement covering rating disputes. An escrow deposit of Rs 50 lakh shall be held with a scheduled commercial bank for the duration of registration.

## 4. Penalties and Withholding

Non-compliance with Clause 3 shall attract a monetary penalty of up to Rs 25 lakh per contravention. The Board may withhold renewal of registration for any provider that fails to submit annual audited controls reports by 30 June of each year.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Existing providers shall seek registration within six months of that date.

This register maps Orion Capital Ltd's internal financial controls to the directors' responsibility statement under Section 134(5)(e) and the audit committee duties under Section 177. The board attests annually, with the report due on 15 July 2025 for FY 2024-25. Each control owner certifies quarterly, and the first certification cycle closes on 30 September 2025.

## Penalty Exposure (Flagged)

- **Primary penalty:** Up to **₹1 crore per contravention** on the Regulated Entity for failing to comply with the beneficial-owner requirement [GRC-01, Para 41; Para 16].
- **Additional PMLA exposure:** The Para 41 penalty applies "in addition to any action under the PMLA" [GRC-01, Para 41]. Under the PMLA Rules extract, Rule 9 requires client identification to follow the Para 16 beneficial-owner requirement [GRC-02, Rule 9]. FIU-IND may impose a penalty of **₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000 per failure** [GRC-02, Section 13].
- **Indicative maximum per contravention:** ₹1 crore (Para 41) plus up to ₹1 lakh per PMLA failure (Section 13), where both are triggered. The corpus supports the cumulative reading through the "in addition to" wording, but it does not state an aggregate cap.

## Obligation Mapping

| Control / Obligation | Source | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Identify beneficial owner of company customers | GRC-01, Para 16 | Identify every natural person holding ≥10% of shares or capital, or exercising control by other means. The earlier 25% threshold was withdrawn from 1 July 2025. |
| Fallback identification | GRC-01, Para 16 | Where no natural person is identified, treat the senior managing official as beneficial owner. |
| CDD at onboarding and on doubt | GRC-01, Para 12 | Carry out CDD at account opening and whenever previously obtained identification data is in doubt. |
| Client identification under PMLA | GRC-02, Rule 9 | Client identification must follow the Para 16 beneficial-owner requirement. |
| Record retention | GRC-02, Rule 9 | Preserve identity and transaction records for 5 years after the relationship ends. |
| Periodic KYC updation | GRC-01, Para 24 | Update records every 2 years (high risk), 8 years (medium risk) or 10 years (low risk). |

## Advisory Observations

1. **Threshold currency:** Advisers should confirm the 10% threshold is applied to all company clients onboarded or reviewed after 1 July 2025. The corpus does not address how legacy 25%-based determinations are to be treated.
2. **Penalty basis:** The corpus says "per contravention" but does not define whether a contravention is a single client, a single account, or a single missed beneficial owner. This is material for quantifying exposure across a portfolio.
3. **Discretion:** The PMLA penalty is framed as a power ("may impose"), so the outcome is discretionary and the corpus gives no guidance on mitigating factors.

## Gaps / Not found in corpus

- Whether the ₹1 crore cap applies per client, per account, per contravention type, or in aggregate across a reporting period.
- The maximum aggregate exposure across multiple non-compliant company clients.
- Any remediation pathway, escrow, or supervisory-fee consequence for KYC/BO failures. (DIST-17 has escrow provisions, but it governs credit-information reporting, not KYC.)
- Mitigating factors or the basis on which FIU-IND sets a penalty within the ₹10,000 to ₹1,00,000 range.
- Treatment of client relationships onboarded before 1 July 2025 under the earlier 25% threshold.
- Any control-attestation or audit-committee certification requirement for KYC/BO controls. (Such requirements appear in DIST-17 and DIST-12, which concern credit reporting and IT outsourcing, not KYC.)

# Circular SYN-7421/13/2025: Related Party Transaction Approval Thresholds under LODR

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to listed entities whose equity shares are traded on a recognised stock exchange. It governs related party transactions (RPTs) entered into by the entity or any of its subsidiaries, including transactions involving transfer of resources, services, or obligations, and any indemnity, guarantee, or escrow arrangement with a related party.

## 2. Approval Thresholds

An RPT exceeding the lower of 2.5 per cent of annual consolidated turnover or INR 1,200 crore requires prior approval of the audit committee and a special resolution of the shareholders. Transactions below this threshold require audit committee approval only. Transactions with a value below INR 10 crore, or below 0.5 per cent of turnover, are exempt from shareholder approval but must be reported quarterly.

## 3. Interested Party Controls

A related party, or any director with a material interest, shall abstain from voting on the relevant resolution. Listed entities shall maintain documented controls, including a withholding of payment pending approval where the transaction has not been cleared, and a fortnightly reconciliation of RPT ledgers.

## 4. Disclosure and Penalties

Entities shall disclose approved RPTs to the exchanges within 2 working days of the approval date. Non-compliance attracts a penalty of INR 25 lakh per instance, with an additional INR 50,000 per day of delay, capped at INR 1 crore per financial year.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026 for transactions entered into on or after that date. Existing arrangements shall be brought into compliance by 30 September 2026.

The corpus names three categories of professional who can certify the share price, and the SPA names a narrower one:

- **FEMA pricing (DEAL-03):** The fair value of shares transferred from a resident to a non-resident must be certified by a **Chartered Accountant, a SEBI-registered merchant banker, or a Registered Valuer**. The price must not be below that fair value, which must be determined under an internationally accepted pricing methodology [DEAL-03, Pricing].
- **Companies Act 2013 valuation (DEAL-01):** The SPA makes a **Registered Valuer's** valuation report under the Companies Act 2013 a condition precedent [DEAL-01, Clause 12(a)].

# FCRA - synthetic extract

## Registration and account
An association or trust may receive foreign contribution only if it holds an FCRA registration, and only into its designated FCRA bank account.

## Foreign source
A foreign company, including a company incorporated outside India such as a Singapore entity, is a foreign source.

## Commercial consideration exception
Money received from a foreign source as **bona fide commercial consideration** (for example the price for shares sold) is **not** foreign contribution, provided that:
1. the price is supported by a valuation report of a **Registered Valuer** under the Companies Act 2013, which must be valid on the date of transfer, and
2. the transaction is reported to the authorities within 30 days.
Where these conditions are not met, the receipt is treated as foreign contribution and requires prior permission, failing which the registration may be cancelled.

## Utilisation
Foreign contribution may be used only for the purposes stated in the registration, and administrative expenses are capped at 20%.

# Client Identity Record Retention After Relationship Exit

## Penalty Flag

**Non-compliance penalty:** For each failure to comply with the PMLA Rules, FIU-IND may impose a monetary penalty of not less than Rs 10,000 and not more than Rs 1,00,000 per failure [GRC-02, Section 13]. The retention obligation itself is set out in Rule 9 [GRC-02, Rule 9].

The source marks this extract as synthetic and states that its rule numbers, periods and penalties are fictional [GRC-02, Header]. The answer below reflects the corpus only.

## Direct Answer

Identity and transaction records must be preserved for **5 years after the business relationship has ended** [GRC-02, Rule 9].

## Control Mapping

| Regulatory Obligation | Source | Required Control Design (Advisory Inference) | Evidence for Audit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Preserve identity and transaction records for 5 years after relationship end | GRC-02, Rule 9 | Retention schedule keyed to the relationship-end date, with a 5-year clock per customer | Retention register showing relationship-end date, retention expiry date, and disposal approval |
| Client identification follows beneficial-owner requirement | GRC-02, Rule 9; GRC-01, Para 16 | Identity records retained should include the beneficial-owner identification performed under Para 16 | Sample of retained files showing BO identification at 10% threshold |

Note: The control design column is an advisory inference. The corpus does not prescribe a specific control.

## Observations

1. **Trigger event:** The retention clock starts when the business relationship ends [GRC-02, Rule 9]. The corpus does not define how the end date is determined, for example on account closure, last transaction, or written notice. Institutions should define this in their own policy.
2. **Scope:** Rule 9 covers both identity records and transaction records [GRC-02, Rule 9].
3. **Penalty linkage:** Para 41 of the KYC Master Direction attaches a separate penalty of up to Rs 1 crore per contravention to failures under Paras 12, 16 and 24, in addition to PMLA action [GRC-01, Para 41]. Retention under Rule 9 is not listed in Para 41, so that specific penalty does not apply to retention failures on the face of the corpus. Rule 9 failures are covered by the FIU-IND penalty in Section 13 of the PMLA extract [GRC-02, Section 13].
4. **Audit workpapers are a different obligation:** GRC-05 states that internal audit workpapers are retained for 8 years [GRC-05, Records]. This applies to audit workpapers, not to client identity records, and does not change the Rule 9 period.

## Gaps / Not found in corpus

- The corpus does not define how the "relationship end" date is determined.
- The corpus does not specify the format, storage medium, or security requirements for retained records.
- The corpus does not state whether retention applies differently to records of relationships that ended before the rule's effective date. No effective date for the PMLA extract is given.
- The corpus does not specify disposal procedures after the 5-year period expires.
- The corpus does not include a penalty specific to retention failures under the KYC Master Direction. Para 41 covers Paras 12, 16 and 24 only [GRC-01, Para 41].
- The corpus does not provide an internal audit test for record retention. GRC-05 tests control IC-KYC-07 (periodic KYC review), not retention [GRC-05, Purpose].

## Penalty Exposure (Flagged First)

- **Non-compliance penalty:** For each failure to comply with the PMLA Rules, FIU-IND may impose a penalty of **Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per failure** [GRC-02, Section 13]. A failure to preserve identity and transaction records falls within "these Rules," so this penalty applies.
- **Related KYC exposure:** Para 41 of the RBI Master Direction sets a penalty of **up to Rs 1 crore per contravention** for failures under Para 12, 16 or 24, "in addition to any action under the PMLA" [GRC-01, Para 41]. Rule 9 is not listed in Para 41, so this penalty does not directly cover a retention failure. It would apply if the retention failure also breached Para 12, 16 or 24.

## Answer

The corpus requires records of identity and transactions to be **preserved for 5 years after the business relationship has ended** [GRC-02, Rule 9].

- **Scope:** The obligation covers both identity records and transaction records [GRC-02, Rule 9].
- **Trigger:** The 5-year period runs from the end of the business relationship, not from the date of a transaction or account opening [GRC-02, Rule 9].
- **Linked obligation:** Client identification under Rule 9 follows the beneficial-owner requirement in Para 16 of the Master Direction [GRC-02, Rule 9; GRC-01, Para 16]. Para 16 sets a **10% beneficial-owner threshold**, with the earlier 25% threshold withdrawn from 1 July 2025 [GRC-01, Para 16].

## Control Mapping

| Control / Procedure | Regulatory Obligation Satisfied | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Rule 9 retention requirement | PMLA Rules, Rule 9 (5-year post-relationship retention) | The obligation itself. No control in the corpus is mapped to it. |
| IC-KYC-07 (tested via SOP-IA-KYC-03) | KYC periodic updation, Para 24 | Tests whether KYC records are refreshed. It does not test retention of records after exit. Not a retention control. |
| SOP-IA-KYC-03 workpaper retention (8 years) | Not a client-record obligation in the corpus | This 8-year period applies to internal audit workpapers, not client identity records. It must not be cited as evidence of compliance with Rule 9. |

**Conclusion on controls:** The corpus contains no control that evidences the 5-year post-exit retention of client identity or transaction records. A dedicated retention control would need to be established and tested.

## Gaps / Not found in corpus

- **Retention control design:** No corpus document describes a control (owner, frequency, evidence) that enforces the 5-year retention period.
- **Retention mechanics:** The corpus does not define how a "business relationship has ended" is determined, or how the 5-year clock is evidenced for multi-product customers.
- **Record format and storage:** No requirements on format, location, or retrievability of retained records are given.
- **STR and CTR records:** Rule 8 (STR filing) and Rule 10 (cash transaction reporting) are present in the corpus, but the corpus does not state retention periods for STR or CTR records.
- **Penalty for retention failure under the Master Direction:** Para 41 does not expressly list Rule 9, so the corpus does not confirm the Master Direction penalty applies to a retention failure alone.
- **Source status:** GRC-01, GRC-02 and GRC-05 are labelled as synthetic, fictional benchmarking documents, not official RBI or PMLA text. Rule numbers, periods and penalties must be verified against official sources before any client-facing or regulatory use.

# Master Direction SYN-RBI/KYC/2025 - Know Your Customer (KYC)

Issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to all Regulated Entities (REs), including banks and NBFCs. Read with the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) Rules.

## Para 12 - Customer Due Diligence (CDD)
REs shall carry out CDD at account opening, and whenever there is doubt about previously obtained identification data.

## Para 16 - Beneficial Owner (BO)
Where the customer is a company, the RE shall identify the beneficial owner: every natural person who, alone or with others, holds ownership of or entitlement to **10% or more** of the shares or capital, or who exercises control through other means.
The earlier threshold of 25% is withdrawn from 1 July 2025.
Where no natural person is identified, the senior managing official shall be treated as the beneficial owner.

## Para 24 - Periodic updation
KYC records shall be updated at least once every:
- 2 years for high-risk customers,
- 8 years for medium-risk customers,
- 10 years for low-risk customers.

## Para 41 - Penalty
Failure to comply with Para 12, 16 or 24 attracts a monetary penalty of up to Rs 1 crore per contravention on the Regulated Entity, in addition to any action under the PMLA.

## Para 45 - Reporting
Suspicious transactions shall be reported as required under the PMLA Rules to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

# SYN-DL/11/2025: Key Fact Statement and Cooling-off Framework for Digital Lending

## 1. Scope and Effective Date
This fictional circular applies to regulated entities and lending service providers offering digital loans through mobile applications, with effect from 1 April 2026. Existing arrangements shall be aligned within 90 days of that date.

## 2. Key Fact Statement
Every borrower shall receive a key fact statement before disbursement. The statement must disclose the all-inclusive annual percentage rate, a processing fee not exceeding 2.5 per cent of the principal, the default penalty rate, and the grievance contact. Acknowledgement shall be recorded through a click-through confirmation.

## 3. Cooling-off Period
A borrower may exit a digital loan without penalty within 3 working days of disbursement, provided the principal and proportionate interest are repaid within that window. No prepayment charge shall apply. Any refund due shall not be withheld beyond 2 working days of receipt.

## 4. Penalties and Controls
Failure to issue the statement or honour the cooling-off right attracts a penalty of up to Rs 5 lakh per instance. Repeated non-compliance within a financial year may lead to restriction on fresh digital lending. Lenders shall maintain an escrow reserve equal to 1 per cent of the outstanding digital loan book, held with a scheduled commercial bank, as an indemnity against borrower refunds.

# Circular SYN-7741/3/2025: Safe-Harbour Margins for IT-Enabled Services

## 1. Scope

This circular applies to eligible assessees providing IT-enabled services to associated enterprises where the aggregate value of such international transactions does not exceed INR 250 crore in the relevant previous year.

## 2. Prescribed Margin

The prescribed safe-harbour margin is 16.25 per cent on operating cost, computed on a cost-plus basis. Where the assessee's operating margin falls below this rate, the variance shall be treated as an adjustment for transfer pricing purposes.

## 3. Option and Filing

An assessee opting into the scheme shall file Form SYN-STP-1 on or before 31 October 2025. The option remains in force for five consecutive assessment years. Withdrawal within the lock-in period attracts a penalty of 2 per cent of the international transaction value.

## 4. Controls and Security

Assessees shall maintain board-approved transfer pricing controls, including a quarterly intercompany reconciliation. Any downward adjustment exposure shall be backed by an indemnity and escrow arrangement with the foreign associate. Failure to maintain such controls shall attract a penalty of INR 5 lakh per default.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect from 1 April 2025 and supersedes Circular SYN-7702/2/2024 in respect of IT-enabled services only.

# Notification SYN-NTF/1/2025: Withholding on Royalty Payments to Non-Residents under Section 94Y

## 1. Scope and Applicability
This notification applies to every Indian resident payer who credits or pays royalty to a non-resident payee in a financial year, whether by cash transfer, adjustment against an intercompany account, or release from an escrow arrangement. Payments for the transfer of rights in a copyrighted article are included.

## 2. Rate and Threshold
Tax shall be withheld at 12 per cent of the gross royalty where the aggregate royalty credited to a single non-resident payee during the financial year exceeds Rs 25 lakh. Once the threshold is crossed, withholding applies to the entire royalty amount credited in that year, not merely the excess.

## 3. Deposit and Filing
Tax withheld shall be deposited with the designated government account by the seventh day of the month following the month of deduction. The payer shall furnish the quarterly statement in the prescribed form within 30 days from the end of each quarter.

## 4. Indemnity and Escrow Holdbacks
Where the payee disputes the applicable rate, the payer may hold the disputed portion in an escrow account for up to 90 days pending a lower-deduction certificate. Any indemnity given to the payee for tax not withheld must be disclosed in the payer's audit file.

## 5. Consequences of Default
Failure to deduct attracts simple interest at 1 per cent per month from the date of deduction to the date of deposit. A penalty equal to the amount not deducted may be levied. This notification takes effect from 1 April 2026; payments under contracts executed before 1 October 2025 remain governed by the earlier regime.

# Advisory Note SYN-CBDT-P/31/2025: Presumptive Taxation Scheme for Small Professionals

## 1. Eligibility

A resident individual or firm engaged in notified professional services may opt into the scheme if gross receipts in the prior financial year do not exceed ₹85 lakh, and cash receipts do not exceed 5 per cent of total receipts. Opt-in is made through the prescribed circular form before the due date of the return.

## 2. Presumptive Income

Deemed income is computed at 48 per cent of gross receipts for eligible professionals. Taxpayers may declare a higher figure only where supported by books of account audited under the notification's prescribed format.

## 3. Withholding and Advance Tax

Payers deducting tax at source on professional fees shall apply a rate of 10 per cent where the payee has furnished a valid scheme declaration. Advance tax is payable in instalments on 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March, with interest at 1 per cent per month on shortfall.

## 4. Penalties and Indemnity

Failure to file the opt-in form within 30 days of the prescribed date attracts a late fee of ₹5,000. Misreporting of receipts exceeding 10 per cent of declared amounts attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax sought to be evaded. Professionals must indemnify the payer against any shortfall arising from an invalid declaration.

## 5. Effective Date

The scheme applies from assessment year 2026-27. Opt-outs may be exercised within 60 days of the start of any financial year.

# Circular No. SYN-4417/6/2025: Refund of Unutilised Input Tax Credit under Inverted Duty Structure

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to registered persons whose input goods or services carry a higher rate of tax than the output supplies, resulting in accumulated unutilised input tax credit. It covers supplies made on or after 1 April 2025 and all refund claims filed under the fictional Notification No. 19/2025-Central Tax.

## 2. Computation of Refund

The refundable amount equals the unutilised credit attributable to inputs, multiplied by the ratio of net turnover of inverted-rated supplies to adjusted total turnover. Claims below Rs 25,000 in a tax period are not admissible.

## 3. Provisional Refund and Withholding

Officers may sanction up to 90 per cent of the claimed amount provisionally. The balance of 10 per cent shall be withheld pending verification, which must conclude within 60 days of filing. Where a discrepancy exceeding 5 per cent is found, the entire provisional amount may be recovered with interest at 18 per cent per annum.

## 4. Indemnity, Escrow and Internal Controls

Claimants seeking provisional refunds above Rs 2 crore must furnish a bank guarantee or deposit an escrow equal to 15 per cent of the excess, and execute an indemnity undertaking covering reversal of wrongful credit. Taxpayers shall maintain documented reconciliation controls and certify monthly ledger tie-outs.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date

A false or inflated refund claim attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax wrongly refunded, subject to a floor of Rs 10,000. This circular takes effect on 15 July 2025.

# Circular No. SYN-CBDT-C/07/2025 (dated 20 August 2025)

Issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to remove doubts on the scope of Section 94Z of the Income Tax Act (synthetic), as amended by Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025.

## 1. Clarification (retrospective)
It is clarified that "cross-border technical and consultancy services" under Section 94Z always included intra-group management service charges, shared-service recharges and cost-sharing recoveries paid to associated non-resident enterprises.
This is a **retrospective clarification** and has effect from 1 April 2023, the date Section 94Z was introduced. It is not a new levy.

## 2. Consequence
Deductors who did not withhold on intra-group management charges in FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 are liable to withhold at the rate then applicable (5%), together with interest at 1.5% per month under Section 94Z(5).

## 3. Penalty relief
Penalty under Section 271Z shall not be levied where the shortfall tax and interest are deposited on or before 31 March 2026.
After that date penalty equal to 100% of the tax not withheld applies.

## 4. Distinction from the Notification
Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025 (10% rate, Rs 50 lakh threshold) operates prospectively from 1 April 2025. This Circular clarifies scope only; it does not change the rate for earlier years.

# Notification No. SYN-CBDT/14/2025 (dated 12 February 2025)

The Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT), Income Tax Department, hereby notifies amendments to Section 94Z of the Income Tax Act (synthetic).

## 1. Rate and threshold (prospective)
Section 94Z requires every person making payment of fees for cross-border technical and consultancy services to a non-resident to withhold tax at source.
- With effect from 1 April 2025, the withholding rate is increased from 5% to 10%.
- The annual aggregate threshold is reduced from Rs 1 crore to Rs 50 lakh per payee per financial year.
- These changes are **prospective** and apply only to payments made on or after 1 April 2025.
- For payments made between 1 April 2023 and 31 March 2025 the earlier rate of 5% and threshold of Rs 1 crore continue to apply.

## 2. Compliance
The deductor shall deposit the tax by the 7th of the following month and file Form 27Z quarterly with the Tax Authority.

## 3. Consequences of default
- Interest under Section 94Z(5) at 1.5% per month on tax not withheld, from the date it was deductible until deposit.
- Penalty under Section 271Z equal to 100% of the tax not withheld.

## 4. Related instruments
The meaning of "cross-border technical and consultancy services" is further clarified in CBDT Circular SYN-CBDT-C/07/2025.

# Circular SYN-7741/3/2025: Safe-Harbour Margins for IT-Enabled Services

## 1. Scope

This circular applies to eligible assessees providing IT-enabled services to associated enterprises where the aggregate value of such international transactions does not exceed INR 250 crore in the relevant previous year.

## 2. Prescribed Margin

The prescribed safe-harbour margin is 16.25 per cent on operating cost, computed on a cost-plus basis. Where the assessee's operating margin falls below this rate, the variance shall be treated as an adjustment for transfer pricing purposes.

## 3. Option and Filing

An assessee opting into the scheme shall file Form SYN-STP-1 on or before 31 October 2025. The option remains in force for five consecutive assessment years. Withdrawal within the lock-in period attracts a penalty of 2 per cent of the international transaction value.

## 4. Controls and Security

Assessees shall maintain board-approved transfer pricing controls, including a quarterly intercompany reconciliation. Any downward adjustment exposure shall be backed by an indemnity and escrow arrangement with the foreign associate. Failure to maintain such controls shall attract a penalty of INR 5 lakh per default.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect from 1 April 2025 and supersedes Circular SYN-7702/2/2024 in respect of IT-enabled services only.

# SYN-4471/23/2025: Advisory Note on Schemes of Arrangement and Merger Approvals

This note summarises fictional procedural controls for schemes proposed under a notional Section 230 framework. It is intended for internal review only.

## 1. Scope and Meeting Thresholds

The scheme applies to a compromise or arrangement between a company and its members or creditors. Approval requires a majority in number, representing at least 70% in value, of those present and voting at the convened meeting. Each class must be separately convened where rights differ materially.

## 2. Filing and Notice Periods

A petition is filed before the Tribunal with a fee of ₹38,500. Notice to the Regional Director and the Official Liquidator must issue within 14 days of filing. Members and creditors receive at least 21 clear days' notice before the meeting, and the notification to the stock exchange must be lodged by 3 March 2025 under circular No. SYN-MCA/12/2025.

## 3. Withholding, Indemnity and Escrow Controls

Where consideration is payable to dissenting shareholders, 2.5% is placed in escrow for 180 days. A 1.5% withholding applies to deemed transfers. The acquirer's indemnity is capped at 10% of the transaction value, with a survival period of 24 months.

## 4. Penalties and Non-Compliance

Failure to file the scheme within the prescribed window attracts a default penalty of ₹75,000, plus ₹2,000 per day of continuing default, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh. Directors of the company are liable jointly for the penalty unless they establish that they acted diligently.

# Share Purchase Agreement Summary: Kestrel Capital and Orion Textiles Ltd (SYN-SPA/21/2025)

## 1. Parties and Consideration

Kestrel Capital (the "Purchaser") will acquire 61.5% of the equity shares of Orion Textiles Ltd (the "Company") for an aggregate consideration of INR 240 crore, subject to the adjustments below. Completion is targeted for 30 September 2025. Tax may be withheld at source on consideration payable to non-resident Sellers.

## 2. Indemnity and Cap

The Sellers indemnify the Purchaser against losses arising from breach of warranty, undisclosed liabilities and pre-completion tax demands. Aggregate liability is capped at 15% of the Purchase Consideration. Individual claims below INR 25 lakh are disregarded, and claim notices must be served within 18 months of completion.

## 3. Escrow

12% of the Purchase Consideration, being INR 28.8 crore, is deposited with an escrow agent for 24 months from completion. Half is released at month 12, provided no claims are pending. The balance is released at month 24, less amounts reserved for open claims.

## 4. Working-Capital Adjustment

Completion accounts are prepared within 60 days. If closing net working capital deviates from the agreed target of INR 46 crore by more than INR 1 crore, the price is adjusted pro rata, subject to a collar of INR 2 crore. Disputes go to an independent chartered accountant, whose determination is final absent manifest error.

## 5. Controls Undertaking

The Company maintains internal financial controls consistent with the Companies Act, 2013. An external compliance review must be delivered by 31 December 2025. Late delivery attracts a penalty of INR 10 lakh per month, payable to the Purchaser.

# SYN-HPL/SHA-41/26/2025: Shareholders Agreement Summary, Helix Pharma Ltd

## 1. Drag-Along Right

Where Promoter Group holders intend to transfer shares representing 58% or more of paid-up equity capital, they may require the remaining shareholders to sell pro rata on identical terms. A drag notice shall be issued at least 30 days before the proposed completion date. Any indemnity given by a dragged shareholder is capped at the consideration that shareholder receives.

## 2. Tag-Along Right

Minority shareholders holding not more than 10% may elect to sell their full holding alongside any Promoter transfer that results in a change of control. The election must be communicated in writing within 14 days of the transfer notice. Five percent of the purchase price shall be held in escrow for 90 days against warranty claims.

## 3. Board Reserved Matters

The following require the affirmative vote of the Investor Director in addition to a simple majority of the Board:

(a) issue of equity or convertible instruments exceeding ₹75 crore in any financial year;
(b) related-party transactions above ₹4 crore;
(c) borrowings exceeding 1.5 times net worth;
(d) any regulatory filing involving renewal of a product licence.

## 4. Default and Penalties

Breach of a reserved matter control attracts a penalty of 2% per month on the amount affected, accruing from the date of breach until cure. Persistent non-compliance for two consecutive quarters entitles the Investor to nominate an additional independent director, effective on notice to the Company Secretary dated 1 April 2026.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

## 2. Duty Rate and Valuation Floor

Share transfer instruments are chargeable at 0.15 per cent of the consideration or the market value of the shares, whichever is higher. Duty on any single instrument shall not fall below ₹250 or exceed ₹1,20,000. Where shares are transferred through a demat account without a separate instrument, the depository participant shall withhold and remit duty on behalf of the transferor within 7 working days.

## 3. Agreements to Sell and Escrow Arrangements

An agreement to sell attracts duty at 0.05 per cent of the agreed consideration. Where part of the consideration is held in escrow, duty is payable on the full amount at the time of execution, and any indemnity or holdback amount must be disclosed in the agreement.

## 4. Impounding and Penalty

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

# FEMA NDI Rules - synthetic extract

## Pricing
A transfer of shares of an Indian company from a resident to a non-resident shall not be at a price less than the fair value determined under an internationally accepted pricing methodology. The fair value shall be certified by a Chartered Accountant, a SEBI-registered merchant banker or a Registered Valuer.

## Deferred consideration and escrow
Up to **25% of the total consideration** may be deferred or held in escrow for a period not exceeding **18 months** from the date of the transfer agreement.

## Reporting
The resident seller or Indian company shall file **Form FC-TRS** with the authorised dealer bank within **60 days** of receipt of the consideration or transfer of shares, whichever is earlier.
Delay attracts compounding under the Foreign Exchange Management Act.

## Sectoral condition
Where the Indian company has a regulated financial subsidiary (such as an NBFC), prior approval of the sectoral regulator may be required for change in control.

# SYN-4471/23/2025: Advisory Note on Schemes of Arrangement and Merger Approvals

This note summarises fictional procedural controls for schemes proposed under a notional Section 230 framework. It is intended for internal review only.

## 1. Scope and Meeting Thresholds

The scheme applies to a compromise or arrangement between a company and its members or creditors. Approval requires a majority in number, representing at least 70% in value, of those present and voting at the convened meeting. Each class must be separately convened where rights differ materially.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

# Circular No. SYN-4417/6/2025: Refund of Unutilised Input Tax Credit under Inverted Duty Structure

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to registered persons whose input goods or services carry a higher rate of tax than the output supplies, resulting in accumulated unutilised input tax credit. It covers supplies made on or after 1 April 2025 and all refund claims filed under the fictional Notification No. 19/2025-Central Tax.

## 2. Computation of Refund

The refundable amount equals the unutilised credit attributable to inputs, multiplied by the ratio of net turnover of inverted-rated supplies to adjusted total turnover. Claims below Rs 25,000 in a tax period are not admissible.

Officers may sanction up to 90 per cent of the claimed amount provisionally. The balance of 10 per cent shall be withheld pending verification, which must conclude within 60 days of filing.
