## 4. Indemnity, Escrow and Internal Controls

Claimants seeking provisional refunds above Rs 2 crore must furnish a bank guarantee or deposit an escrow equal to 15 per cent of the excess, and execute an indemnity undertaking covering reversal of wrongful credit. Taxpayers shall maintain documented reconciliation controls and certify monthly ledger tie-outs.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date

A false or inflated refund claim attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax wrongly refunded, subject to a floor of Rs 10,000. This circular takes effect on 15 July 2025.

# Advisory Note SYN-7741/10/2025: GST Rate on Electric-Vehicle Charging Services

## 1. Background
The 56th GST Council, at its fictional sitting of 14 October 2025, considered whether charging services supplied through public electric-vehicle chargers should attract a concessional rate. The Council recommended 12 per cent for registered suppliers, subject to issue of a notification.

# Advisory Note SYN-CBIC/88/2025 on Composition Levy Eligibility for Small Manufacturers

## 1. Aggregate Turnover Ceiling

A registered person engaged in the manufacture of goods may opt for the composition levy where aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year does not exceed ₹96,00,000. For taxpayers in designated special-category States, the ceiling is ₹48,00,000. Turnover is computed on a PAN-wide basis for the purposes of this illustration.

## 2. Supply Restrictions

Composition dealers shall not make inter-State outward supplies or supplies through an e-commerce operator that collects tax at source. Supplies of specified edible preparations attract a fixed levy of 2.5 per cent of turnover in the State, effective from 1 April 2025 under Notification SYN-N/12/2025.

## 3. Option Filing and Reversal of Credit

Intimation in Form SYN-CMP/1 must be filed on or before 15 May 2025 for the current year. Where input tax credit has been availed on capital goods, a reversal equal to 10 per cent of the value of such goods is required on the date of opting in. Failure to reverse attracts a penalty of ₹25,000.

## 4. Loss of Eligibility and Liability Escrow

Where turnover exceeds the ceiling during a year, the person ceases to be eligible from the day the threshold is crossed and must pay tax at normal rates on stock held. Interest at 18 per cent per annum applies to delayed payment. Management is advised to maintain monthly turnover controls and an escrow reserve equal to 5 per cent of projected turnover against this contingent liability.

With effect from 1 April 2025 (prospective), any registered person that wishes to distribute input tax credit on common input services (for example head-office audit, IT or management services) to its branches or distinct persons must obtain registration as an Input Service Distributor (ISD) under Rule 39A.

# Advisory Note SYN-GST/7/2025: Reverse Charge on Residential Rent Paid to Registered Persons

Under the fictional 55th Council recommendation, where a registered person takes a residential dwelling on rent for use by its employees, the recipient shall discharge GST under reverse charge at 12 per cent on rent paid to an unregistered landlord. Late self-assessment attracts interest at 18 per cent per annum and a penalty of Rs 10,000 per return period. Recipients should obtain an indemnity from landlords and place an escrow of Rs 2 lakh against disputed liabilities.

# Advisory Note SYN-CBIC/88/2025 on Composition Levy Eligibility for Small Manufacturers

## 1. Aggregate Turnover Ceiling

A registered person engaged in the manufacture of goods may opt for the composition levy where aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year does not exceed ₹96,00,000. For taxpayers in designated special-category States, the ceiling is ₹48,00,000. Turnover is computed on a PAN-wide basis for the purposes of this illustration.

## 2. Supply Restrictions

Composition dealers shall not make inter-State outward supplies or supplies through an e-commerce operator that collects tax at source. Supplies of specified edible preparations attract a fixed levy of 2.5 per cent of turnover in the State, effective from 1 April 2025 under Notification SYN-N/12/2025.

## 3. Option Filing and Reversal of Credit

Intimation in Form SYN-CMP/1 must be filed on or before 15 May 2025 for the current year. Where input tax credit has been availed on capital goods, a reversal equal to 10 per cent of the value of such goods is required on the date of opting in. Failure to reverse attracts a penalty of ₹25,000.

## 4. Loss of Eligibility and Liability Escrow

Where turnover exceeds the ceiling during a year, the person ceases to be eligible from the day the threshold is crossed and must pay tax at normal rates on stock held. Interest at 18 per cent per annum applies to delayed payment. Management is advised to maintain monthly turnover controls and an escrow reserve equal to 5 per cent of projected turnover against this contingent liability.

# Circular No. SYN-4417/6/2025: Refund of Unutilised Input Tax Credit under Inverted Duty Structure

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to registered persons whose input goods or services carry a higher rate of tax than the output supplies, resulting in accumulated unutilised input tax credit. It covers supplies made on or after 1 April 2025 and all refund claims filed under the fictional Notification No. 19/2025-Central Tax.

## 2. Computation of Refund

The refundable amount equals the unutilised credit attributable to inputs, multiplied by the ratio of net turnover of inverted-rated supplies to adjusted total turnover. Claims below Rs 25,000 in a tax period are not admissible.

## 3. Provisional Refund and Withholding

Officers may sanction up to 90 per cent of the claimed amount provisionally. The balance of 10 per cent shall be withheld pending verification, which must conclude within 60 days of filing. Where a discrepancy exceeding 5 per cent is found, the entire provisional amount may be recovered with interest at 18 per cent per annum.

## 4. Indemnity, Escrow and Internal Controls

Claimants seeking provisional refunds above Rs 2 crore must furnish a bank guarantee or deposit an escrow equal to 15 per cent of the excess, and execute an indemnity undertaking covering reversal of wrongful credit. Taxpayers shall maintain documented reconciliation controls and certify monthly ledger tie-outs.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date

A false or inflated refund claim attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax wrongly refunded, subject to a floor of Rs 10,000. This circular takes effect on 15 July 2025.

# Circular SYN-7421/13/2025: Related Party Transaction Approval Thresholds under LODR

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to listed entities whose equity shares are traded on a recognised stock exchange. It governs related party transactions (RPTs) entered into by the entity or any of its subsidiaries, including transactions involving transfer of resources, services, or obligations, and any indemnity, guarantee, or escrow arrangement with a related party.

## 2. Approval Thresholds

An RPT exceeding the lower of 2.5 per cent of annual consolidated turnover or INR 1,200 crore requires prior approval of the audit committee and a special resolution of the shareholders. Transactions below this threshold require audit committee approval only. Transactions with a value below INR 10 crore, or below 0.5 per cent of turnover, are exempt from shareholder approval but must be reported quarterly.

## 3. Interested Party Controls

A related party, or any director with a material interest, shall abstain from voting on the relevant resolution. Listed entities shall maintain documented controls, including a withholding of payment pending approval where the transaction has not been cleared, and a fortnightly reconciliation of RPT ledgers.

## 4. Disclosure and Penalties

Entities shall disclose approved RPTs to the exchanges within 2 working days of the approval date. Non-compliance attracts a penalty of INR 25 lakh per instance, with an additional INR 50,000 per day of delay, capped at INR 1 crore per financial year.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026 for transactions entered into on or after that date. Existing arrangements shall be brought into compliance by 30 September 2026.

# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

# Master Direction SYN-RBI/KYC/2025 - Know Your Customer (KYC)

Issued by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to all Regulated Entities (REs), including banks and NBFCs. Read with the Prevention of Money Laundering (PMLA) Rules.

## Para 12 - Customer Due Diligence (CDD)
REs shall carry out CDD at account opening, and whenever there is doubt about previously obtained identification data.

Where the customer is a company, the RE shall identify the beneficial owner: every natural person who, alone or with others, holds ownership of or entitlement to **10% or more** of the shares or capital, or who exercises control through other means.
The earlier threshold of 25% is withdrawn from 1 July 2025.
Where no natural person is identified, the senior managing official shall be treated as the beneficial owner.

## Para 24 - Periodic updation
KYC records shall be updated at least once every:
- 2 years for high-risk customers,
- 8 years for medium-risk customers,
- 10 years for low-risk customers.

## Para 41 - Penalty
Failure to comply with Para 12, 16 or 24 attracts a monetary penalty of up to Rs 1 crore per contravention on the Regulated Entity, in addition to any action under the PMLA.

## Para 45 - Reporting
Suspicious transactions shall be reported as required under the PMLA Rules to the Financial Intelligence Unit-India (FIU-IND).

# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

Prepared for Axiom Holdings Pte Ltd on the proposed acquisition of Meridian Components Ltd (aggregate annual

Finding 1 - Withholding on intra-group management fees

E-invoicing is not enabled in the Company's ERP.

At 38 company customers, a beneficial owner holding between 10% and 25% was not identified, because the control still
applies the withdrawn 25% threshold. Potential penalty up to Rs 1 crore per contravention (up to Rs 38 crore in
aggregate).
Finding 5 - Meridian Foundation
The Foundation (8% shareholder) is FCRA-registered. No valuation report has yet been obtained for its shares.
Recommendations
Rely on the SPA tax indemnity (clause 9.4) for Findings 1 and 2; require Sellers to pay the Section 94Z shortfall before
31 March 2026; remediate the KYC control before Closing; obtain a Registered Valuer report dated within 90 days of the
transfer.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

## 2. Duty Rate and Valuation Floor

Share transfer instruments are chargeable at 0.15 per cent of the consideration or the market value of the shares, whichever is higher. Duty on any single instrument shall not fall below ₹250 or exceed ₹1,20,000. Where shares are transferred through a demat account without a separate instrument, the depository participant shall withhold and remit duty on behalf of the transferor within 7 working days.

## 3. Agreements to Sell and Escrow Arrangements

An agreement to sell attracts duty at 0.05 per cent of the agreed consideration. Where part of the consideration is held in escrow, duty is payable on the full amount at the time of execution, and any indemnity or holdback amount must be disclosed in the agreement.

## 4. Impounding and Penalty

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

# State Stamp Duty Circular SYN-4417/30/2025: Share Transfer Instruments and Agreements to Sell

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to share transfer instruments and agreements to sell executed in the State on or after 1 April 2026. Instruments executed outside the State are chargeable if received within the State within 45 days of execution.

## 2. Duty Rate and Valuation Floor

Share transfer instruments are chargeable at 0.15 per cent of the consideration or the market value of the shares, whichever is higher. Duty on any single instrument shall not fall below ₹250 or exceed ₹1,20,000. Where shares are transferred through a demat account without a separate instrument, the depository participant shall withhold and remit duty on behalf of the transferor within 7 working days.

## 3. Agreements to Sell and Escrow Arrangements

An agreement to sell attracts duty at 0.05 per cent of the agreed consideration. Where part of the consideration is held in escrow, duty is payable on the full amount at the time of execution, and any indemnity or holdback amount must be disclosed in the agreement.

## 4. Impounding and Penalty

An instrument found under-stamped shall be impounded. The deficit duty is recoverable together with a penalty of 2 per cent per month of the deficit, subject to a cap of 100 per cent of the duty payable.

## 5. Effective Date and Compliance Controls

Parties and counsel shall maintain a stamping control register recording the instrument date, duty paid, challan number and escrow details. Non-compliance noticed in any audit under the controls framework will be notified on or before 31 March 2027.

# Companies Act 2013 - valuation provisions (synthetic extract)

## Section 247 - Valuation by Registered Valuer
Where a valuation of shares or assets is required, it shall be made by a Registered Valuer (RV) who is independent of the company and the transaction parties.

## Valuation report content
The report shall state:
- the valuation date and the methodology used (discounted cash flow, net asset value, or market multiples) and the reasons for choosing it,
- key assumptions, and
- the fair value per share.

## Validity
A valuation report is valid for **90 days** from the valuation date. A transaction completed after that period requires a fresh or refreshed report.

## Penalty
A Registered Valuer who knowingly makes a false or misleading valuation shall be punishable with a fine of not less than Rs 1 lakh and up to Rs 5 lakh.

## Use under other laws
A valuation report by a Registered Valuer under this Act is accepted as evidence of fair value for pricing of share transfers under FEMA and for establishing that a transfer is a bona fide commercial transaction under foreign contribution rules.

Disputes go to an independent chartered accountant, whose determination is final absent manifest error.

## 5. Controls Undertaking

The Company maintains internal financial controls consistent with the Companies Act, 2013. An external compliance review must be delivered by 31 December 2025. Late delivery attracts a penalty of INR 10 lakh per month, payable to the Purchaser.

# Circular SYN-7421/13/2025: Related Party Transaction Approval Thresholds under LODR

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to listed entities whose equity shares are traded on a recognised stock exchange. It governs related party transactions (RPTs) entered into by the entity or any of its subsidiaries, including transactions involving transfer of resources, services, or obligations, and any indemnity, guarantee, or escrow arrangement with a related party.

## 2. Approval Thresholds

An RPT exceeding the lower of 2.5 per cent of annual consolidated turnover or INR 1,200 crore requires prior approval of the audit committee and a special resolution of the shareholders. Transactions below this threshold require audit committee approval only. Transactions with a value below INR 10 crore, or below 0.5 per cent of turnover, are exempt from shareholder approval but must be reported quarterly.

## 3. Interested Party Controls

A related party, or any director with a material interest, shall abstain from voting on the relevant resolution. Listed entities shall maintain documented controls, including a withholding of payment pending approval where the transaction has not been cleared, and a fortnightly reconciliation of RPT ledgers.

## 4. Disclosure and Penalties

Entities shall disclose approved RPTs to the exchanges within 2 working days of the approval date. Non-compliance attracts a penalty of INR 25 lakh per instance, with an additional INR 50,000 per day of delay, capped at INR 1 crore per financial year.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026 for transactions entered into on or after that date. Existing arrangements shall be brought into compliance by 30 September 2026.

> **PENALTY ALERT (flagged first per GRC guardrail)**
> - **KYC penalty:** Failure to comply with Para 16 (beneficial owner identification) attracts a penalty of up to **Rs 1 crore per contravention** on the Regulated Entity (RE), in addition to any PMLA action [GRC-01, Para 41].
> - **PMLA penalty:** For each failure to comply with the PMLA Rules, including Rule 9, FIU-IND may impose a penalty of **Rs 10,000 to Rs 1,00,000 per failure** [GRC-02, Section 13].

A single beneficial-owner identification failure may therefore engage both regimes. The corpus does not explicitly confirm that both penalties stack for the same act (see Gaps).

---

## 1. How the Two Rules Connect

**Rule 9 imports the KYC standard.** Under the PMLA Rules, client identification "shall follow the beneficial-owner requirement in Para 16 of Master Direction SYN-RBI/KYC/2025" [GRC-02, Rule 9]. The PMLA client identification obligation therefore does not set its own beneficial-owner test. It takes the test from the KYC Master Direction.

**The beneficial-owner test (Para 16).** Where the customer is a company, the RE must identify:
- every natural person who, alone or with others, holds ownership of or entitlement to **10% or more** of the shares or capital; or
- every natural person who exercises control through other means [GRC-01, Para 16].
- The earlier 25% threshold was withdrawn from 1 July 2025 [GRC-01, Para 16].

**Record retention.** Identity and transaction records must be preserved for **5 years after the business relationship ends** [GRC-02, Rule 9].

**CDD trigger.** CDD is required at account opening and "whenever there is doubt about previously obtained identification data" [GRC-01, Para 12]. This is the point at which beneficial-owner data should be re-verified.

# SYN-RBI-CR/17/2025: Credit Information Reporting by Lenders to Credit Information Companies

## 1. Scope and Reporting Entities

This circular applies to all regulated lenders holding aggregate exposure of ₹5 crore or more with any borrower. Lenders must furnish account-level data to every credit information company (CIC) with which they have an active membership agreement.

## 2. Submission Frequency and Data Standards

Lenders shall submit data monthly, on or before the 7th day of the succeeding month. Each record must carry a unique account identifier, a days-past-due field accurate to the nearest day, and the outstanding principal. Records with suit-filed or written-off status must be reported within 3 working days of the event.

## 3. Correction Window and Borrower Disputes

Where a borrower disputes an entry, the lender shall verify and respond within 21 calendar days. Corrections must be transmitted to all CICs within 2 working days of verification. Lenders retain indemnity obligations for losses caused by erroneous submissions.

## 4. Penalties for Non-Compliance

A failure to submit by the due date attracts a penalty of ₹10,000 per day of delay, subject to a cap of ₹5 lakh per reporting cycle. Repeated defaults in any two consecutive quarters may result in escrow of supervisory fees pending remediation.

## 5. Effective Date and Transition

This circular takes effect on 1 April 2026. Lenders must submit a controls attestation, certified by the board audit committee, by 30 June 2026.

# Circular SYN-XXXX/14/2025: Cyber Resilience Framework for Stock Brokers

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to all stock brokers whose average monthly client base exceeds 25,000 unique accounts. Brokers below this threshold shall comply with the controls in Annexure B within nine months of the notification date, being 1 April 2026.

## 2. Incident Reporting

Any cyber incident affecting trading systems, client data or order routing shall be reported to the exchange within 3 hours of detection, followed by a root-cause note within 15 days. Failure to report attracts a monetary penalty of Rs 2,00,000 per instance, with a further Rs 25,000 for each day of continued default.

## 3. Controls and Testing

Brokers shall conduct vulnerability assessments every quarter and penetration testing twice in each financial year through an empanelled auditor. Critical findings must be closed within 30 days. Repeated lapses shall result in withholding of 5% of incentives payable to the designated officer until remediation is certified.

## 4. Indemnity and Vendor Obligations

Brokers using third-party cloud or software vendors shall obtain a contractual indemnity covering losses arising from vendor-originated breaches. The indemnity shall be backed by an escrow deposit equal to 6% of annual contract value, held for 12 months from the date of the incident.

## 5. Effective Date

This circular takes effect from 1 April 2026. Existing vendor contracts shall be amended to conform within 90 days of that date.

# Meridian: E-Invoicing Applicability and IRN Rule for Credit-Distribution Documents

## Summary

1. **E-invoicing applicability cannot be determined from the corpus.** The corpus sets the threshold but contains no Meridian turnover figure. Meridian's AATO must be confirmed against the threshold.
2. **Credit-distribution documents (ISD invoices) must carry an IRN and QR code from 1 January 2026.** This is a prospective requirement [TAX-04, §3]. The corpus does not state that this obligation is subject to the AATO threshold (see Point 3 below).

## 1. E-Invoicing Threshold (Prospective)

- E-invoicing is mandatory for every registered person whose AATO exceeds Rs 5 crore, down from Rs 10 crore, effective 1 January 2026 [TAX-04, §1]. The consolidated table reflects the same threshold [TAX-05, E-invoicing row].
- Meridian's turnover is not stated in any source. Applicability therefore depends on whether Meridian's AATO exceeds Rs 5 crore. This must be confirmed from Meridian's books.
- Failure to issue an e-invoice attracts a penalty of 100% of tax due or Rs 10,000, whichever is higher, per invoice [TAX-04, §5].

## 2. IRN Rule for Credit-Distribution (ISD) Documents

**Rule:** ISD invoices issued for distribution of input tax credit must carry an IRN and QR code from 1 January 2026 [TAX-04, §3].

Supporting provisions:

- **Credit may be distributed only by ISD invoice.** Distribution by ordinary invoice, journal entry or internal debit note is not valid [TAX-03, §2].

# Advisory Note SYN-CBIC/88/2025 on Composition Levy Eligibility for Small Manufacturers

## 1. Aggregate Turnover Ceiling

A registered person engaged in the manufacture of goods may opt for the composition levy where aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year does not exceed ₹96,00,000. For taxpayers in designated special-category States, the ceiling is ₹48,00,000. Turnover is computed on a PAN-wide basis for the purposes of this illustration.

## 2. Supply Restrictions

Composition dealers shall not make inter-State outward supplies or supplies through an e-commerce operator that collects tax at source. Supplies of specified edible preparations attract a fixed levy of 2.5 per cent of turnover in the State, effective from 1 April 2025 under Notification SYN-N/12/2025.

## 3. Option Filing and Reversal of Credit

Intimation in Form SYN-CMP/1 must be filed on or before 15 May 2025 for the current year. Where input tax credit has been availed on capital goods, a reversal equal to 10 per cent of the value of such goods is required on the date of opting in. Failure to reverse attracts a penalty of ₹25,000.

## 4. Loss of Eligibility and Liability Escrow

Where turnover exceeds the ceiling during a year, the person ceases to be eligible from the day the threshold is crossed and must pay tax at normal rates on stock held. Interest at 18 per cent per annum applies to delayed payment. Management is advised to maintain monthly turnover controls and an escrow reserve equal to 5 per cent of projected turnover against this contingent liability.

# Circular No. SYN-CBDT-C/07/2025 (dated 20 August 2025)

Issued by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) to remove doubts on the scope of Section 94Z of the Income Tax Act (synthetic), as amended by Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025.

## 1. Clarification (retrospective)
It is clarified that "cross-border technical and consultancy services" under Section 94Z always included intra-group management service charges, shared-service recharges and cost-sharing recoveries paid to associated non-resident enterprises.
This is a **retrospective clarification** and has effect from 1 April 2023, the date Section 94Z was introduced. It is not a new levy.

## 2. Consequence
Deductors who did not withhold on intra-group management charges in FY 2023-24 and FY 2024-25 are liable to withhold at the rate then applicable (5%), together with interest at 1.5% per month under Section 94Z(5).

## 3. Penalty relief
Penalty under Section 271Z shall not be levied where the shortfall tax and interest are deposited on or before 31 March 2026.
After that date penalty equal to 100% of the tax not withheld applies.

## 4. Distinction from the Notification
Notification SYN-CBDT/14/2025 (10% rate, Rs 50 lakh threshold) operates prospectively from 1 April 2025. This Circular clarifies scope only; it does not change the rate for earlier years.

SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT FOR BENCHMARKING. NOT OFFICIAL TEXT. All figures are fictional.

# Circular No. SYN-4417/6/2025: Refund of Unutilised Input Tax Credit under Inverted Duty Structure

## 1. Scope and Applicability

This circular applies to registered persons whose input goods or services carry a higher rate of tax than the output supplies, resulting in accumulated unutilised input tax credit. It covers supplies made on or after 1 April 2025 and all refund claims filed under the fictional Notification No. 19/2025-Central Tax.

## 2. Computation of Refund

The refundable amount equals the unutilised credit attributable to inputs, multiplied by the ratio of net turnover of inverted-rated supplies to adjusted total turnover. Claims below Rs 25,000 in a tax period are not admissible.

## 3. Provisional Refund and Withholding

Officers may sanction up to 90 per cent of the claimed amount provisionally. The balance of 10 per cent shall be withheld pending verification, which must conclude within 60 days of filing. Where a discrepancy exceeding 5 per cent is found, the entire provisional amount may be recovered with interest at 18 per cent per annum.

## 4. Indemnity, Escrow and Internal Controls

Claimants seeking provisional refunds above Rs 2 crore must furnish a bank guarantee or deposit an escrow equal to 15 per cent of the excess, and execute an indemnity undertaking covering reversal of wrongful credit. Taxpayers shall maintain documented reconciliation controls and certify monthly ledger tie-outs.

## 5. Penalties and Effective Date

A false or inflated refund claim attracts a penalty of 100 per cent of the tax wrongly refunded, subject to a floor of Rs 10,000. This circular takes effect on 15 July 2025.
